{{Short description|Dutch-American businessman}}
'''Marijn Emmanuel Dekkers''' (born 22 September 1957 in [[Tilburg]], [[Netherlands]]) is a Dutch-American scientist and biopharmaceutical businessman. He was [[CEO]] of [[Bayer|Bayer AG]] from 2010 to 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bayer.com/en/dr.-marijn-dekkers.aspx|title=CV of Dr. Marijn Dekkers|last=AG|first=Bayer|website=www.bayer.com|access-date=2016-05-02}}</ref> He was CEO of Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. from 2002 to 2009. He was Chairman of [[Unilever]] from 2016 to 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unilever.com/about/who-we-are/our-leadership/Dr-Marijn-Dekkers.html|title=Dr Marijn Dekkers|website=Unilever global company website|access-date=2016-05-02}}</ref> He is also Founder and Chairman of Novalis LifeSciences LLC, an investment and advisory firm for the Life Science industry he founded in 2017.

== Early life ==

Dekkers grew up as the youngest of three children of a merchant in the Dutch city of Tilburg. After attending local schools, St. Aloysius (primary school) and St. Odulphus (Lyceum), in 1976 he began studying [[chemistry]] at the [[Radboud University Nijmegen|Radboud University in Nijmegen]]. Three years later he began studying chemical technology at [[Eindhoven University of Technology]], where he received his master's degree and PhD in [[chemical engineering]].<ref>Title of Thesis: ''The Deformation Behaviour of Glass Beaded-Filled Glassy Polymers''</ref>

== Career ==
In 1985 Dekkers worked for [[General Electric]] (GE) in different research departments located in the US and the Netherlands. In 1988, he became Research Director of the GE range of [[polymers]] and subsequently held management positions in various other polymer units.

In 1995, Dekkers joined [[Allied Signal]] (later named [[Honeywell International]] Inc.) and took over the management of various business units.

In 2000, he became COO at the Boston-based [[Thermo Electron Corporation]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/boston/blog/mass-high-tech/2009/09/thermo-fisher-ceo-dekkers-leaves-to-head.html|title=Thermo Fisher CEO Dekkers leaves to head Bayer; Casper appointed CEO|website=www.bizjournals.com|access-date=2018-06-06}}</ref> one of the world's leading specialists in the manufacture of laboratory instruments. Within a short time, Dekkers implemented a complete corporate reorganization and became President and CEO in 2002.
In this role, he initiated further extensive restructuring measures, divesting various organizational units and strengthening the company's core business by means of targeted acquisitions, including the purchase in 2006 of the laboratory consumables supplier [[Fisher Scientific]]. After the acquisition, the company renamed as [[Thermo Fisher Scientific]], which employed 30,000 people in six business groups.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2006/05/08/AR2006050800325_pf.html?noredirect=on|title=Thermo Electron, Fisher Scientific in Deal|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=2018-06-06|language=en-US|issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

On 1 January 2010 Dekkers was appointed to the board of Bayer AG and on 1 October 2010 he took over as CEO from [[Werner Wenning]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.fiercebiotech.com/press-releases/dr-marijn-e-dekkers-be-new-ceo-bayer-october-1-2010 | title=Dr. Marijn E. Dekkers to be new CEO of Bayer from October 1, 2010 &#124; FierceBiotech| date=15 September 2009}}</ref> On 3 June 2014 Bayer AG announced that its Supervisory Board had extended Marijn Dekkers' term as CEO by two years, on expiration of the initial five-year period. Dekkers cited family reasons for extending his contract only until the end of 2016.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.fiercepharma.com/story/bayer-ceos-long-goodbye-dekkers-depart-end-2016/2014-06-03 | title=Bayer CEO's long goodbye: Dekkers to depart at end of 2016 &#124; FiercePharma}}</ref> He left Bayer on 30 April 2016 before the controversial Monsanto acquisition and was succeeded by Werner Baumann on 1 May 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bayer.com/en/werner-baumann.aspx|title=Bayer's CEO: Werner Baumann|last=AG|first=Bayer|website=www.bayer.com|access-date=2016-05-02}}</ref> During Dekkers' tenure as CEO he strongly emphasized innovation.  Bayer became the company with the largest market capitalization in the German DAX 30 index, and held that position for approximately three years until his departure from the company in April of 2016.

Since April 2016 he was the Chairman of [[Unilever]] until November 2019.<ref>[https://fd.nl/ondernemen/1324257/geen-nederlander-meer-in-top-tandem-unilever Geen Nederlander meer in top-tandem Unilever ]</ref>

In 2017 Dekkers founded Novalis LifeSciences LLC, an investment and advisory firm for the Life Science industry (www.novalislifesciences.com).

== Controversy ==

In 2013 some controversy was sparked during a ''Financial Times'' panel discussion with relation to Bayer's kidney and liver cancer drug [[Nexavar]].<ref>The original quote causing the debate was "''Is this going to have a big effect on our business model? No, because we did not develop this product for the Indian market, let’s be honest. We developed this product for Western patients who can afford this product, quite honestly. It is an expensive product, being an oncology product.''" – [https://www.cjr.org/the_audit/bloombergs_viral_misquote_1.php Columbia Journalism Review, January 29, 2014], [https://www.ft-live.com/ft-events/ft-global-pharmaceuticals-biotechnology-conference-2013/sessions/buffering-the-pharma-brand-restoring-reputation-rebuilding-trust-panel Videorecording of the panel (19:00 – 19:30)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141111214816/https://www.ft-live.com/ft-events/ft-global-pharmaceuticals-biotechnology-conference-2013/sessions/buffering-the-pharma-brand-restoring-reputation-rebuilding-trust-panel |date=2014-11-11 }}</ref>

He spoke at a conference in 2014, saying<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cjr.org/the_audit/bloombergs_viral_misquote_1.php | title=Bloomberg's viral misquote}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://keionline.org/node/1924 | title=Transcript of Bayer CEO Marjin Dekkers quote at the December 3, 2013 FT Event, regarding India compulsory license of Nexavar| date=2014-02-07}}</ref>{{Quotation|"So now, is this going to have a big effect on our business model? No, because we did not develop this product for the Indian market, let's be honest. I mean, you know, we developed this product for Western patients who can afford this product, quite honestly."<ref>{{cite web| url=http://keionline.org/node/1910| title=Bayer CEO Marijn Dekkers explains: Nexavar cancer drug is for "western patients who can afford it."| date=2014-01-23| access-date=2014-11-22| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140124111754/http://keionline.org/node/1910| archive-date=2014-01-24| url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ft-live.com/ft-events/ft-global-pharmaceuticals-biotechnology-conference-2013/sessions/buffering-the-pharma-brand-restoring-reputation-rebuilding-trust-panel |title=Buffering the Pharma Brand: Restoring Reputation, Rebuilding Trust - PANEL &#124; Calendar &#124; FT Live |accessdate=2014-11-20 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141111214816/https://www.ft-live.com/ft-events/ft-global-pharmaceuticals-biotechnology-conference-2013/sessions/buffering-the-pharma-brand-restoring-reputation-rebuilding-trust-panel |archivedate=2014-11-11 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Pharma-drug-development-only-for-wealthy-countries/articleshow/29456711.cms | title=Pharma drug development only for wealthy countries? - Times of India| website=[[The Times of India]]}}</ref>}}

[[Médecins Sans Frontières]] responded to Dekkers' comment, saying that it {{Quotation|sums up everything that is wrong with the multinational pharmaceutical industry. Bayer is effectively admitting that the drugs they develop are deliberately going to be rationed to the wealthiest patients.<ref>http://www.msfaccess.org/content/msf-response-bayer-ceo-statement-medicines-developed-only-western-patients. {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141220064348/http://www.msfaccess.org/content/msf-response-bayer-ceo-statement-medicines-developed-only-western-patients |date=2014-12-20 }}</ref>}} Dekkers replied to this, referring to the decision made by the Indian government, not to protect a patent on Nexavar and the intellectual property of Bayer. He also said: {{Quotation|I regret that what was a quick response from me within the framework of a panel discussion at the recent FT Pharma conference has come across in a different way as it was meant by myself. It could not be more opposite to what I want and we do at Bayer.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnlamattina/2013/12/05/does-pharma-only-develop-drugs-for-those-who-can-pay/?commentId=comment_blogAndPostId/blog/comment/2009-1298-1228 | title=Does Pharma Only Develop Drugs for Those Who Can Pay?| website=[[Forbes]]}}</ref>}}
